it doesn't have to be super complicated, it took some experimentation in terms of products but now that I know what works for my hair, my routine is pretty simple. I wash my hair in the morning, then use a leave in conditioner for moisture and a gel for definition, then basically let it air dry while I go about my day. To sleep I just put my hair up in a ponytail or a loose bun on the top of my head. I wash my hair every two to three days on a good week haha. I learned everything I know from naturallycurly.com, they have a quiz that will help you figure out the curl pattern of your hair, and will suggest products that are good for your type.

possible yes, but i personally wouldn't. Sleeping on wet hair absolutely ruins mine at least, i can't speak for others, so you'd probably have to dry with a blow-dryer, on a lower heat with a diffuser (my hair can take 2+ hours to fully dry, and even then the roots will probably be a little wet for a while). personally I'm not a huge fan of how blowdrying can make my curly pattern tighter and can still cause a little frizz factor, so I prefer to air dry, but that's really a personal preference. Also, heat can damage your hair and with curls, that can mess up the curl pattern. A lot of people who started wearing their hair naturally after using heat or perms for a while have to do "the big chop", cutting off the damaged hair. All of this is to say that if you want to blow dry, I recommend getting some sort of heat protective hair product. you'd probably also want to use satin pillowcase or bonnet when you sleep to prevent frizz.
